description.value: The study examined whether fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex in adolescent boys with ADHD affected error-monitoring activation, stop-task performance, and clinical symptoms, compared with active neurofeedback of the left parahippocampal gyrus.

design.value: The study was a single-blind randomised controlled trial investigating the effect of fMRI-NF of the rIFC in 18 boys with ADHD (rIFC-NF group) compared to an active control group of 13 boys with ADHD (lPHG-NF group). Participants underwent fMRI stop-task assessment before and after neurofeedback training.

task_description.value: The fMRI-NF protocol consisted of four 1 h to 1.15 hr sessions within a 2-week period, totalling a maximum of 14 NF runs of 8.5 min each. Each run consisted of 6 activation blocks of 40 s, separated by a rest block of 30 s. The run started with a rest block showing an image of a dolphin. During activation blocks, neurofeedback of the target region was represented by a video of a rocket, which participants were asked to move toward space using any strategy they could.

instructions.value: Minimal instructions were given. Participants were asked to move the rocket toward space using any strategy they could and were informed or reminded of the delay of at least 6 s in the feedback.

stimuli.value: A video of a rocket during activation blocks and an image of a dolphin during the initial rest block; a score based on distance travelled was displayed after each activation/training block.

task_performance_measures.value: fMRI-NF performance score (0–10), based on the distance travelled during each run

task_description.value: The tracking stop task is a choice reaction time task investigating motor response inhibition and error monitoring. Participants responded as fast as they could to arrows pointing left or right. In 20% of trials, the go signal was followed by a stop signal and participants had to inhibit their response. The task consisted of 156 go trials and 40 stop signals, with stop signals appearing about 250 ms after the go signal. A tracking algorithm changed the interval between go and stop signal onsets according to each subject’s inhibitory performance, resulting in 50% successful and 50% unsuccessful inhibition trials in each run.

design_type.value: choice reaction time task with pseudo-randomly distributed stop-signal trials

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to respond as fast as they could to arrows pointing left or right and to inhibit their response when a stop signal appeared.

stimuli.value: Arrows pointing left or right as go signals and stop signals following some go signals.

description.value: The continuous feedback was updated every MRI repetition time, based on the change in BOLD response in the target ROI compared with a white matter reference ROI. The target ROIs were the rIFC and lPHG, depending on group.

description.value: Details of the acquisition of the fMRI stop task were available in Alegria et al. (2017) and the supplementary material, but are not provided in the reported text.
A T1-weighted structural image was used to map the target ROIs defined in Talairach space to individual participant fMRI scans.
A two-volume EPI localizer image was collected at the start of each session and used with the T1-weighted structural image to map target ROIs to individual participant fMRI scans.
The real-time fMRI data were transferred and analysed for neurofeedback; the mean BOLD signal was extracted from target and white matter reference ROIs using masks applied to pre-processed fMRI data.

Extraction of mean BOLD signal from each ROI

description.value: The fMRI data underwent realignment, motion correction, smoothing, global detrending and spin-excitation history correction. The individual time series were analysed with a wavelet-based data resampling method.

software.value: Version 4.1 of the non-parametric XBAM software package

model_settings.value: Pre- and post-fMRI-NF effects were tested within and between groups for clinical outcome measures and stop-task dependent variables.

The experimental condition of error monitoring, failed stop trials, was contrasted against an implicit baseline of go trials. Individual goodness-of-fit statistic (SSQ-ratio) maps were created and transformed into standard space.

software.value: Version 4.1 of the non-parametric XBAM software package

model_settings.value: A repeated-measures ANOVA tested the interaction of time (pre, post) by group (rIFC-NF group, lPHG-NF group). The voxel-level threshold was p < 0.05 and the cluster-level threshold was p < 0.02, determined by direct permutation; cluster mass rather than cluster extent was used.

software.value: Version 4.1 of the non-parametric XBAM software package

model_settings.value: A group activation map across all participants was produced for the fMRI-NF condition contrasted with the baseline condition, averaged across all 11 runs. A voxel-wise test at p < 0.05 was followed by a cluster-level threshold of p < 0.011; the text also reports p < 0.001 for cluster-level comparisons.

software.value: Version 4.1 of the non-parametric XBAM software package

model_settings.value: Post-versus-pre fMRI-NF brain activation changes were correlated with corresponding post-versus-pre changes in post-error reaction time and ADHD-RS clinical outcome measures in the rIFC-NF group.
